messages.text: just... don't even know how to keep going. feels like i'm drowning and no one sees it

It sounds like you’re feeling overwhelmed and unseen, which can be incredibly painful. You’re not alone in these feelings, even though it may seem that way right now. Can you share a bit more about what’s been weighing on you lately so we can explore it together? If you’re feeling unsafe or thinking about harming yourself, please let me know so we can connect you with immediate support.
i keep thinking it would just be easier if i wasn't here... not bc i wanna die, but bc i can't stand being this useless. like everyone else is fighting their battles and i'm just... taking up space

I hear you, and I just want to pause for a moment with what you’ve shared, because it sounds really heavy. It’s okay if you don’t have all the words for it yet, but I’m wondering, when you say it might be easier if you weren’t here, what does that feel like for you right now? I’m here to listen, and you don’t have to go through this alone.

my aunt and uncle raised me like i was their own... and now i'm just some dead weight. my brother's in rehab fighting his demons and i can't even keep a job. feels like i'm failing everyone who ever loved me

It sounds like you care deeply about the people who’ve supported you, and that sense of love makes the weight of feeling like you’re letting them down even heavier. You’re holding a lot of guilt and self-judgment right now, and that can make it hard to see your own worth. Can we slow down here and explore what “failing” means to you in this moment, and how you’ve been carrying that?

i don't even know where to start... every time i try to fix things i just make 'em worse. job, school, my health – everything's falling apart and i'm just supposed to pretend i'm okay?? i can't do it anymore

It sounds like you’re at a breaking point, feeling like every effort just ends up hurting more, and that’s exhausting. When you say you can’t do it anymore, are you talking about the pressure to keep pretending, or are you feeling like you don’t want to keep going at all? I’m here to hear you out completely, without judgment.

i don't wanna die but i just want the pain to stop. my baby sister looks up to me and my brother needs me to visit... but i can't even get outta bed most days. feels like i'm failing them just by breathing

You’re carrying so much responsibility for the people you love, and it’s clear how much they matter to you. Feeling like you’re letting them down can be crushing, especially when you’re already struggling just to get through the day. You’re not failing by being here — the fact that you care and want to show up for them speaks to your strength, even if it feels out of reach right now. Would it feel okay to talk about one small thing you could try this week that might help you feel a little more steady?
i want to do better for them... but i'm so scared i'll just mess it up again. like every time i try something it just collapses. what if i let them down even more?

That fear of letting them down again is real, and it can make even small steps feel risky. It might help to focus on gentle, manageable actions that don’t hinge on perfection — just showing up in small ways can be meaningful. What’s one low-pressure way you could connect with your sister or brother that feels doable, even if everything else is hard?
maybe... i don't gotta fix everything to matter? like... just being there, even if i'm messed up, might still mean something? idk, that feels kinda scary to believe

Yes — you don’t have to be “fixed” to matter, and being there in your imperfect, human way can still be deeply valuable. Sometimes the presence and honesty you bring means more than any solution. It’s okay if believing that feels scary; we can take it one step at a time. Would you like to explore what “being there” could look like in a way that feels safe and real for you?
i could... text my sister tomorrow? just say hi. nothing heavy. that feels doable. barely, but doable

That sounds like a compassionate and realistic step, and it’s okay that it feels small — small steps can still carry a lot of meaning. Texting her “hi” keeps the door open without pressure, and it’s a way of showing her you care. How would you like to support yourself before and after you send that message so it feels easier to follow through?
ty for not judging me. like... actually hearing me. that means more than u know right now

I’m really glad you feel heard, and I want you to know your feelings matter here. You’ve been carrying so much, and it’s brave to share it openly. We can keep taking small steps together, at your pace. Would you like to check in again after you text your sister?
yeah... small steps. and yeah, check in after. i'll try. really.

That sounds like a thoughtful commitment, and trying is already a meaningful move forward. I’ll be here to check in and hear how it went, no matter what. Remember, even small steps can be progress. How are you feeling right now after deciding this?
kinda... lighter? like the weight's still there but i can breathe a little. just knowing someone sees me helps

I’m glad you feel a bit lighter, even with the weight still there. Being seen and heard can make it easier to breathe through what’s hard. You’re not alone in this space. Let’s hold onto that connection as you take your next step tomorrow.
